overall: The AG found two violations: the opening open session of the October 5 meeting was not accessible to the public, and minutes of the August 17 meeting were not timely approved. The town-by-law filing claim was declined.

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged the Board failed to follow proper procedure entering executive session at its October 5 meeting; the opening open session was not accessible to the public.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board failed to provide public access to this portion of the meeting, which the public was entitled to view, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged the Board failed to timely approve both open and executive session minutes of its August 17 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As the October 5 meeting was six meetings, and more than 30 days, after the August 17 meeting, we find that the Board failed to timely approve both the open and executive session minutes of the August 17 meeting.

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged executive session minutes were not filed with the Town Clerk within the timeframe required by a town by-law.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
